newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Spring/White Wheat - Spring wheat bids lower.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Spring/White Wheat - Spring wheat bids lower.

text.p: Cash bids for dark northern spring wheat weakened in response to lower Minneapolis Grain Exchange futures and increased country movement, traders said.

Grain dealers in Montana said Monday's temperatures were in the 50s (degrees Farenheit), which allowed rail movement to catch up from last week's snow- and cold-related delays. But dealers said farmer selling remained slow.
"The railroads are starting to spot cars again, but it's just not a very strong market at the moment. There's no business," a Montana dealer said.
Dealers also warned that another winter storm was expected to hit the northern Plains by midweek.
MGE March wheat settled 1-1/2 to five cents per bushel lower, with March down five cents at $3.80-1/4.
Bids for 14 percent protein spring wheat for January delivery into Portland, Ore., were eight cents per bushel lower than Friday's closing bids.
USDA's Market News Service said the bids were lower on the decline in MGE March wheat and on adequate supplies in the pipelines to meet nearby exporter demand.
